title: Etcd raft apply delay -> leadership failover -> autoscaler surge (on-call notes)
content:
Summary:

Short summary: On 2024-11-03 at ~09:17 UTC we observed a cluster-wide increase in API server 5xx errors and HPA churn. Root surface: a sustained increase in etcd apply latency (~200-800ms p99 for ~12 minutes) that triggered raft leadership elections and a window of degraded quorum availability. The HPA controllers interpreted pod CPU/req metrics inconsistently during the window and issued a burst of scale operations, creating a feedback loop that exacerbated API server load.

Impact:
- ~6 minutes of degraded control-plane availability (API server 500/503 spikes).
- ~15 HH: several workloads experienced delayed rollouts; some k8s controllers retried causing spikes in etcd write QPS.
- HPA-triggered scale-ups led to ~120 additional Pod create attempts across 8 namespaces, increasing scheduler pressure and leading to transient pending pods.
- No user-facing inference traffic timeouts recorded (data plane isolated), but internal CI job failures and platform deploys impacted.

Detection / Alerting:
- Pager triggered by etcdctl:etcd_apply_latency.p99 > 300ms for 1m at 09:18 UTC (alert SRE-ETCD-APPLY-LATENCY).
- API server error-rate alert fired at 09:19 UTC.
- HPA-churn metric alert (HPA_ops > 20/min) fired at 09:21 UTC.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 09:16:30 — Background compaction job started on etcd member etcd-2 (scheduled daily).
- 09:17:10 — etcd apply latency begins climbing (p99 ~350ms).
- 09:18:50 — Pager: etcd p99 alert. First on-call (Aisha) acknowledges.
- 09:19:10 — API server 5xx surge starts; request queueing observed in apiserver metrics.
- 09:20:05 — Observed raft leadership transfer: etcd-2 -> etcd-1 (logs show leader stepdown after slow apply).
- 09:21:00 — HPA churn alert; K8s controllers issue repeated updates creating more etcd writes.
- 09:22:30 — Mitigations executed (see below).
- 09:28:00 — etcd apply latency p99 drops below 100ms; leadership stabilizes.
- 09:31:00 — API error rate returns near baseline; follow-up tasks created.

What we ran / quick debug notes:
- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd -o wide -> confirmed etcd-2 had higher restart count (older).
- ssh to etcd-2 (10.1.64.22) -> dmesg showed intermittent io scheduler stalls around 09:16.
- journalctl -u etcd -o short-precise | sed -n '55800,55860p' -> repeated \"slow apply\" messages and increased follower read latency.
- etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.1.64.21:2379,https://10.1.64.22:2379,https://10.1.64.23:2379 endpoint status -> confirmed leader is etcd-1 during the window; etcd-2 lagging.
- metrics: etcd_mvcc_compaction_duration_seconds spike correlates with maintenance compaction.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:22–09:26):
1) Temporarily pause automated compaction job for cluster (cronjob disabled) — Marcus. Rationale: background compaction coincided with peak.
2) Throttled HPA controller reconciliation frequency by setting controller-lease-duration and scaling down controller-manager concurrency (targeted temporary change) — Priya. This reduced churn from controllers.
3) Cordoned etcd-2 from scheduling any new system-level pods and moved non-critical control-plane workloads (none were scheduled primarily) — Diego.
4) Increased apiserver write/long-running request queue capacity and rate-limit adjustments to reduce 503s during follow-up (fast fallback) — Aisha.

Root cause hypothesis:
Primary: Background compaction job executed on etcd-2 while the node experienced transient IO latency (EBS gp2 I/O credit exhaustion pattern observed in cloud provider metrics). Compaction is write-heavy and caused apply latency to spike. Because apply latency was high on one follower and leader election was sensitive to timeouts, raft elected a new leader which resulted in short quorum instability.
Secondary contributing factor: HPA/controller-manager aggressive retry/backoff behavior during API errors caused a control-loop amplification. Controller-manager default concurrency and HPA reconcile periods made it easy for controllers to hammer the API when they saw transient failures, increasing etcd write QPS and prolonging recovery.

Why this caused more visible API errors:
- API server depends on stable etcd writes for mutating requests; slow applies cause request timeouts in apiserver (500/503).
- Leadership transfers add additional replication overhead.
- Controller retries increased write load (create/update operations) which fed back into etcd latency.

Post-incident actions and runbook changes (owner + ETA):
1) Runbook: Add "If etcd_apply_latency.p99 > 300ms and compaction jobs ran in last 10m" section with steps: pause compaction, reduce controller concurrency, and temporarily rate-limit HPA. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2024-11-10.
2) Observability: Add per-member etcd disk latency (iops/latency) to etcd dashboards and tie an alert to EBS credit/throughput exhaustion patterns. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2024-11-17.
3) Infrastructure: Move etcd data volumes to gp3 with provisioned IOPS baseline (or add burst-protection). Owner: Diego. ETA: 2024-12-01 (coord with infra schedule).
4) Controller resilience: Implement smoothed HPA scale limits (burst window) and add controller-manager dynamic backoff config to avoid immediate retry storms. Owner: Platform team (PR in linked_artifacts). ETA: 2024-11-24.
5) Chaos testing: Add a synthetic test that runs compaction on a single etcd member while saturating disk to observe failover behavior. Owner: SRE-DR team. ETA: 2025-01-05.

Runbook patch (draft snippet to add to confluence):
- Detect: etcd_apply_latency.p99 > 300ms AND etcd_mvcc_compaction_duration_seconds > 0.
- Immediate steps:
  * Pause compaction cronjob(s) in infra namespace (kubectl scale cronjob compaction -n infra --replicas=0)
  * If compaction was manually triggered, abort if possible (check process / systemd).
  * Reduce controller-manager concurrency: patch deployment kube-system/controller-manager to set --concurrent-deployments=2 (temporary).
  * Set HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 300 for critical HPAs (or patch with kubectl patch hpa <name>).
- If etcd member shows io_scheduled_stalls in dmesg, escalate to infra and consider moving volume or resizing IOPS.

Open questions / follow-ups to investigate:
- Why did compaction land on etcd-2 at this exact time? Was scheduling random or part of maintenance rotation? (Action: check compaction cron scheduling logic)
- Could we stagger compaction across members to avoid coincident heavy writes? (Action: compaction orchestration proposal)
- Are our current etcd timeouts/heartbeat/raft settings optimal for cloud-backed disks with occasional IO spikes?

Commands / quick references used during the incident:
- etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.1.64.21:2379,https://10.1.64.22:2379,https://10.1.64.23:2379 --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt endpoint status
- journalctl -u etcd -o short-precise | grep -i \"slow apply\" -n
- kubectl -n kube-system describe pod etcd-2
- aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name VolumeQueueLength --start-time 2024-11-03T09:00:00Z --end-time 2024-11-03T09:30:00Z --period 60 --namespace AWS/EBS --statistics Average --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0abcd1234

Postmortem notes (to be filled into JIRA SRE-1217):
- Title: Etcd apply latency spike during compaction led to leadership churn and control-plane amplification via HPA.
- Severity: Sev3 (control-plane degraded; no user-facing data-plane impact).
- Timeline: attached above.
- Root cause: compaction-on-member + transient IO credit exhaustion + aggressive controller retries.
- Corrective actions: infrastructure change to gp3, runbook patch, controller/HPA config changes, chaos test.

Appendix (logs snippets):
- etcd log excerpt (sanitized):
  \"2024-11-03T09:17:24.128Z etcdserver: failed to apply entry, took 512ms\"
  \"2024-11-03T09:20:07.435Z raft: leader 10.1.64.21 stepped down\"
  \"2024-11-03T09:20:08.112Z etcdserver: restored leadership, applied index 3456789\"

- apiserver metric snapshot (abridged):
  apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket{verb=\"create\"} p95 ~ 1.2s during spike

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to make compaction safer on cloud disks — gp2 can be deceptive. We should prefer provisioning baseline io for control-plane stateful storage.
- The HPA burst behavior was the surprise: it amplified the problem significantly. Consider short-term global HPA stabilization config for the cluster.

Owners and next checkpoints:
- Priya (runbook + controller changes) — check-in 2024-11-12.
- Marcus (observability + dashboards) — check-in 2024-11-18.
- Diego (infra volume migration plan) — check-in 2024-11-27.

If anything is unclear in the timeline above ping me (Aisha) in #sre-infra or assign to JIRA-SRE-1217.

-- end of notes --
